subject.title: [Bug]: tools/sandbox: MEDIA_MAX_BYTES (5 MB) is hardcoded and not user-configurable

question: Should the remaining 5 MiB media-store and sandbox-staging boundary stay fixed, reuse existing mediaMaxMb/channel caps, or gain a new bounded media-store config contract?
rationale: The code path is source-reproducible, but changing a default resource cap or adding a new config surface affects security, disk usage, operator expectations, and upgrade behavior beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Reuse existing bounded caps
options.body: Thread agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb and channel/account mediaMaxMb through the affected staging paths with explicit upper bounds, docs, and tests so users get one familiar knob.

options.title: Keep core cap fixed
options.body: Land only narrow owner-approved exceptions such as Telegram document delivery and leave generic sandbox/media-store staging at 5 MiB for safety.

options.title: Add a new media-store cap
options.body: Introduce a new canonical config field with schema, docs, upgrade notes, and security review if maintainers want a separate storage/staging limit.

recommendation.title: Reuse existing bounded caps
recommendation.body: Thread agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb and channel/account mediaMaxMb through the affected staging paths with explicit upper bounds, docs, and tests so users get one familiar knob.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved boundary is the sandbox/media-store safety contract, and the history points to Peter Steinberger for the staging split and current main ownership signals.
